root.label: Newcastle vehicle crash into rugby fans

events.label: Newcastle vehicle crash into rugby fans

slots.name: injured count
slots.sentence: Ten people were injured, including two critically, in Australia on Saturday after a car crashed into a crowd of rugby fans lining the streets to send off their team, in what officials called a "horrific" incident.

slots.name: critical condition
slots.sentence: Of the 10 people who were injured, two of them -- a 5-year-old girl and a 67-year-old man -- were taken to the hospital and remain in critical condition, New South Wales police said in an update.

slots.name: stable condition
slots.sentence: The others, including another 5-year-old girl and a 2-year-old girl, were taken to the hospital and were in stable condition, according to police.

slots.name: driver arrest status
slots.sentence: The ages of the other people who were hurt ranged from 24 to 63.

slots.name: road closure status
slots.sentence: Police said the incident closed Newcastle Link Road in both directions and impacted the planned route of the procession.

slots.name: terror relation status
slots.sentence: "Police have commenced an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident, with initial inquiries indicating it is not believed to be terror related," police said in an update.

slots.name: time of crash
slots.sentence: It happened about 9:30 a.m. Saturday local time in Newcastle, about 100 miles north of Sydney, as crowds of thousands of people were lining the street to see off the Newcastle Knights' rugby team, which was headed to Sydney for the grand final later Saturday, officials said.

slots.name: driver age
slots.sentence: The 18-year-old driver was arrested at the scene, police said.
